name: PoisonSeed
iocPatterns: Phishing emails spoofing Microsoft Teams/WhatsApp/Signal invitation URLs
Device‑code authentication URLs capturing token requests
Microsoft Graph API endpoints for message search and exfiltration
Proxy IP addresses matching regionally appropriate hosts
Malicious domains such as login.microsoftonline.com, mailchimp-sso.com, sso-account.com
Keyword searches in emails for credential or admin terms
keyCapabilities: Device‑code phishing via spoofed Microsoft Teams/WhatsApp/Signal invitations
Capture of authentication tokens (device‑code flow, refresh tokens) using client IDs
Use of captured tokens to access accounts and leverage Microsoft Graph API for data harvesting
Lateral movement through spear‑phishing links within an organization
Credential theft from compromised CRM/email providers to send cryptocurrency seed phrase spam
recommendedActions: Educate staff to recognise phishing that mimics messaging apps and verify the authenticity of device‑code authentication prompts
Implement policy controls to restrict device‑code flows to trusted applications only
Monitor Microsoft Authentication Broker logs for unauthorized client IDs and suspicious device‑code requests
Enforce MFA across all accounts and establish conditional access policies that trigger re-authentication on high-risk actions
Revoke compromised refresh tokens via revokeSignInSessions if suspected phishing activity is detected
Leverage Microsoft Graph API monitoring to detect abnormal message search or exfiltration patterns
campaignsText: PoisonSeed’s most recent known campaign, observed in August 2024, involved a large‑scale device-code phishing attack that leveraged familiar collaboration platforms to bypass MFA and acquire tokens. The operation targeted clients across Europe, North America, Africa, the Middle East, and Asia, spanning sectors including government, defense, healthcare, telecommunications, energy/oil & gas, finance, IT services, education, and retail. Using regionally based proxies, the attackers concealed their origin while employing stolen CRM credentials to dispatch spam laden with cryptocurrency seed phrases. They routinely harvest email data via Microsoft Graph API after initial infection and use lateral movement techniques such as spear‑phishing links to expand reach within victim networks.
description: PoisonSeed, a suspected Russia‑aligned threat actor, uses device-code phishing messages masquerading as Microsoft Teams, WhatsApp and Signal invites to harvest MFA authentication tokens and access target accounts via the Microsoft Graph API. The group also extracts credentials from compromised CRM and bulk email platforms to distribute spam containing stolen cryptocurrency seed phrases, thereby generating financial gains for the actors. Operations have been observed across multiple continents, targeting a wide spectrum of sectors including finance, government, health, critical infrastructure and technology.
goals: PoisonSeed primarily seeks to monetize its operations through cryptocurrency theft, leveraging stolen credentials and MFA tokens to compromise accounts and send mass spam containing seed phrases. By targeting high‑profile sectors such as government, defense, healthcare, critical infrastructure, finance, and IT services, the actor not only gains financial rewards but also expands its foothold for further data exfiltration. The broad geographic reach—north of the Atlantic through Asia, Africa, and the Middle East—as well as its use of localized proxies indicate a strategic objective to remain undetected while building a wide footprint that can be subsequently leveraged for political or commercial espionage.
